headline: October core CPI came in hot at 0.3%, the level Fed Governor Waller said this morning would put a half point hike on the table; Nasdaq futures fell about 1%, the 10 year rose to about 4.94%, and Anthropic set terms for an IPO of up to $64.4 billion.
summary: Prices are Monday Nov 9 closes; the dashboard (prices_as_of 2026-11-09) and Massive agree. Monday was a big but thin rebound: QQQ rose 3.54% to 679.35 on the lightest volume of the last four sessions and stopped 0.64% under its 683.69 correction line. This morning BLS said October CPI rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, against 0.2% expected for core, and before the release Waller said a 0.3% core month should bring a 50 basis point hike into the December debate. After the data Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.2%, the 10 year yield near 4.94% and the 2 year near 4.69% (Yahoo, CoinDesk). Treasury sells $42 billion of 10 year notes at 1pm ET, and bonds are closed Wednesday. The put screen passes one idea, the APH $72.50 Dec 18 put, but it should wait until after the auction.

regime.why: The one number traders had, monthly core CPI, came in hot, and a Fed governor had already said that would justify talk of a half point hike. Monday's rally did not reclaim QQQ's 683.69 line and came on light volume, so this morning's drop meets a market that never turned. Brent under $90 is the one real relief.

signals.title: Core CPI prints 0.3%, the number Waller tied to a half point hike
signals.since_yesterday: The print is out: core rose 0.3% in October, above the 0.2% forecast, and Waller said hours earlier that a core reading around 0.3% or higher means a 50 basis point hike should be considered in December.
signals.what_happened: BLS said October CPI rose 0.4% (seasonally adjusted) and core 0.3%. Energy rose 0.7%, food 0.5%, shelter 0.3% and gasoline 1.0%. The only 12 month rate published was gasoline, up 37.4%; headline and core yearly rates were withheld because of the 2025 shutdown gap (BLS). Forecasts were 0.3% headline and 0.2% core; September was 0.6% and 0.3% (CoinDesk). Speaking in London before the release, Waller said he would back a 25 basis point hike in December and that a 50 basis point move should be considered if core came in around 0.3% or higher; he also said hiking only 25 could put the Fed's credibility at risk (Hawksmoor and Yahoo; the text was not found on the Fed site). After the data the 10 year was near 4.93% to 4.94% and the 2 year near 4.69%, up about 14 basis points (CoinDesk, Yahoo). CME FedWatch had a December hike above 80% (Yahoo); a 50 basis point probability was not found.
signals.so_what: A 0.3% core month, held for a year, is about 3.7% inflation, far from 2%. Two months in a row at 0.3% makes the Fed's choice 25 or 50, not hike or hold. Second order: the 2 year moved twice as much as the 10 year, so markets now price a faster, shorter fight. That hurts the most expensive growth stocks first and helps the dollar. Third order: the 1pm ET auction asks buyers to take $42 billion of 10 year notes right after a hot print, and with bonds closed Wednesday any weak result sits for a day. What would make this wrong: a soft November report, or Fed leaders other than Waller pushing back on 50.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries today. Puts: premiums should rise today; sell nothing before the 1pm ET auction result. Long term: AEP is the buy zone name hurt most by higher yields; wait for tonight's refresh before adding.

signals.title: Anthropic sets IPO terms: up to $64.4 billion, plus $26 billion from its own chip and cloud suppliers
signals.what_happened: Anthropic's updated draft prospectus offers 825 million shares at $70 to $78, raising up to $64.4 billion, sold by the company and some holders. A separate $26 billion private placement at the IPO price comes from Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC, for up to $90.4 billion in all. The top of the range values it near $1.02 trillion, below the $1.5 trillion discussed earlier and close to its $965 billion private value. Q3 revenue was $16.96 billion, up 47% from Q2, and compute commitments are nearly $900 billion, including with Amazon and Google. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead; the ticker will be ANT on Nasdaq; no pricing date was given (Reuters, Nov 10).
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the suppliers are buying stock in their biggest customer, which locks in demand for their chips and cloud. Who gets paid: Broadcom, Google, AMD, Micron and TSMC, through $900 billion of compute orders. Who pays: other AI stocks, because a deal this size needs about $64 billion of fresh buying, and funds often sell what they own to make room. The lower valuation is a useful signal too: buyers are pushing back on price in a falling tech market. What would make this wrong: the deal is cut or delayed, which would say AI funding is tightening.
signals.for_you: No action. None of the suppliers has a buy verdict today; AVGO and AMD are watch names, and TSM is #1 on the Lineup with no verdict. Expect AI names to stay jumpy into the pricing, which reports point to around the week of Nov 16 (not confirmed).

signals.title: Nvidia: a new report on chips routed through China, and ARK bought the drop
signals.since_yesterday: Reuters, citing The Information, reported that the relationship behind the board probe helped route at least $7.5 billion of Nvidia chips through Chinese firms. NVDA fell 4.3% Monday on 3.8 times normal volume.

Reuters, citing The Information, reported the chip routing figure; Nvidia had not confirmed it, so treat the number as reported, not proven. NVDA traded near 175.80 after CPI, down 1.6% (Yahoo). ARK's five active ETFs bought about 90,400 NVDA shares on Nov 9, roughly $16 million at the close (ARK trade notice).
signals.so_what: The story is moving from a personal scandal to an export control question, which is the part that can change Nvidia's business. Washington now has a dollar figure to point at. ARK buying is small next to Nvidia's size and is not insider buying. The Nov 17 report and the Nov 18 House briefing remain the two dates that matter.

signals.title: Earnings: Hims loses subscribers, Rocket Lab delays Neutron, Occidental cuts debt; CoreWeave tonight
signals.what_happened: Hims and Hers: revenue $890.4 million, up 49%, but subscribers fell about 100,000 from Q2 to 2.788 million, gross margin fell to 57% from 74%, a net loss of $33.0 million, and a third cut to 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance, now $257 million to $277 million (8-K; StockTitan). HIMS had already fallen 11.8% to 22.94 Monday and traded near 22.64 after CPI (Massive; Yahoo). Rocket Lab: record revenue of $267.8 million, up 73%, backlog $3.57 billion, but Neutron's first launch is now no earlier than 2027 (8-K); RKLB traded near 53.30, down 9.5% from 58.86 (Yahoo). Occidental: adjusted EPS $1.91, $2.8 billion of free cash flow before working capital, debt down $1.8 billion to $10.0 billion (8-K); OXY closed 55.76. AST SpaceMobile: Q3 revenue $42.3 million; about 45 satellites in orbit now targeted for mid 2027, not end of 2026 (8-K). CoreWeave reports after the close today; CRWV closed 48.98.
signals.so_what: The theme is the same across all four: the business grows, but the date or the margin slips, and the stock pays for it. Hims shows the cost of cash pay GLP-1 growth: more revenue, fewer subscribers, thinner margin. Rocket Lab's backlog says demand is real, but the rocket that would earn the big launches is late. CoreWeave tonight is the test that matters most for the AI build, because it borrows to buy chips while yields are rising.
signals.for_you: No action. HIMS moved to 'Wait' and sits under its 26.32 to 29.16 zone; no put. RKLB is rated Avoid. CRWV and ASTS have no usable verdict. Do not trade CRWV into tonight.

signals.title: Rockwell Automation's CEO buys about $1.5 million of stock
signals.what_happened: Rockwell's CEO filed a Form 4 on Nov 9 (EDGAR). The dashboard reads it as an open market buy of about $1.55 million at $386.36 on Nov 9, raising his stake about 4%. The last open market buy by him that we found was in February 2024 (TipRanks). ROK closed 389.36 on Nov 9, up 3.6%, on 1.44 million shares (Massive). It is #19 on the Lineup and in the robotics and defense themes. Other recent buys in the data: two TTM Technologies directors bought about $0.94 million on Nov 5 near $62 to $63, after the CEO and a director bought near $88 to $90 on Oct 28 (TTMI closed 75.33); a TSMC director bought about $0.30 million on Nov 5 (dashboard).
signals.so_what: A CEO who usually sells, buying with his own money right after a 10% monthly drop, is the strongest kind of insider signal: he knows the order book. Factory automation is where the robotics money lands first. What would make this wrong: a pre planned trade or an option related move; we confirmed the filing exists but could not open the form itself.

history.when: February 1994 to February 1995: the Fed's surprise tightening
history.what: The Fed raised its target from 3% to 6% in a year (Fisher Investments), including half and three quarter point moves, and US bond losses reached about $600 billion through the third quarter of 1994 (Fortune).
history.lesson: When the Fed moves faster than the market expects, bonds and the most rate sensitive stocks take the first hit. The economy can still be fine; prices reset first.

history.when: October 1 to November 12, 2025: the federal funding lapse
history.what: BLS never published most October 2025 CPI indexes, so October 2026 has no yearly rate (BLS).
history.lesson: With one number to read, the market reacts to it more. Today the monthly core did the work a yearly rate would have done.

cycle.differences: In 1994 the Fed started from a low 3% rate and inflation was near 3%. Today the Fed is already at 3.75% to 4.00%, inflation is running near 3.7% annualized, and oil is falling, which can cool the headline rate in a few months. A half point hike would be about speed, not about rates being far too low.
